title: Existential suffix after a quantified prefix
statement: Let $q$ be a finite list of existential or universal quantifiers, let $T$ be a CNF formula over natural-number variables, let $G\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $P$ be a predicate on Boolean assignments to natural-number variables. Suppose the variable count of $T$ is at most the length of $q$ plus $G$, and for every assignment $\sigma$, there is an assignment agreeing with $\sigma$ on all variables below the length of $q$ that satisfies $T$ if and only if $P(\sigma)$. Then the quantified formula with prefix $q$ followed by $G$ existential quantifiers, starting from the all-false assignment at index $0$, is true if and only if applying prefix $q$ to $P$ from that same initial assignment is true.
